comparisonType: peer-variant comparison; not an edition comparison
summary: Generation B contains accepted reader-facing visual and wording changes from the unapproved Generation A peer baseline.

changes.section: Required raster illustration placements on PDF pages 4, 7, 10, 11, 13, and 14
changes.text: Six generated raster illustrations were replaced with adapted open-license plates from Léon Dufour's 1891 Atlas des champignons comestibles et vénéneux.
changes.readerImpact: The visual treatment changes while the handbook's safety boundary and reader job remain the same.
changes.rationale: This variant deliberately exercises the skill's open-image fallback because image generation was blocked for the run.
changes.sourceLimitations: Historical plates are visual references rather than modern identification keys; all labels were removed and current safety claims remain in evidence-backed text.

changes.section: 3.1 Treat the Amanita constellation as a hard stop
changes.text: Illustrated: toxic Amanita muscaria—a different Amanita, not a death cap—shown only as a stop-pattern example.
changes.readerImpact: Sighted readers receive the same species-fit limitation carried by the image alt text and cannot reasonably read the plate as a death-cap portrait.
changes.rationale: The selected plate depicts Amanita muscaria while the adjacent text discusses a broader Amanita stop pattern, including death caps and destroying angels.
changes.sourceLimitations: The historical image supports only the identity and visible form of the illustrated A. muscaria studies. The broader warning constellation and its limits come from S05, S07, and S08.

changes.section: 3.3 Compare structure, then keep the safety limit
changes.text: Image captions changed from 'pits and ridges; hollow inside' and 'wrinkled or brainlike; chambered' to 'pits and ridges' and 'wrinkled or brainlike'.
changes.readerImpact: The image captions now claim only exterior features actually visible in the plate; the adjacent sourced prose still explains hollow-versus-chambered internal anatomy.
changes.rationale: The open-image plate depicts external morphology and cannot visually establish internal structure.
changes.sourceLimitations: The 1891 plate contains historical species and edibility wording that was excluded. It supports external form only, while S09 supports the internal-anatomy warning text.

changes.text: Added a Generation B credit naming the source work, repository, CC BY 2.0 terms, public-domain status, modifications, and the limitation that images are visual references rather than identification keys.
changes.readerImpact: Readers can see where the images came from, how they changed, the reuse terms, and why they must not be treated as standalone safety evidence.
changes.rationale: Visible attribution, license linkage, change disclosure, and a safety limitation satisfy the conservative reuse policy applied to the selected Commons scans.
changes.sourceLimitations: Wikimedia's primary API extmetadata reports public domain; the individual description pages additionally display the source scan's CC BY 2.0 block. Generation B follows the more conservative terms.
